items.title: Nonce – Open-source, least-privilege Gmail access for AI agents
items.raw_excerpt:
Hi HN! We built nonce, an open-source tool that sits between personal AI agents (Muse, Grok, ChatGPT, Claude) and your personal data in Gmail, Calendar, Drive and more. Today, if you connect Gmail to an AI agent like Muse, it can read your entire inbox. Whether on purpose or not, they can read far more emails than needed. This poses a huge data-privilege risk, in which personal data is accessed without limits. With nonce, the AI will no longer hold your Google or Slack tokens. To read anything, it has to show its intent first: User's question: When does my flight to Tokyo leave?
Agent's justification: Need the airline confirmation email
Agent's search query: from:united.com Tokyo
Access needed: 10 minutes If the justification and search query are reasonable, nonce issues a scoped token to

items.title: Building an AI Traffic Guardrail(kilasec)
items.raw_excerpt: Show HN: An AI traffic guardrail Building something based on 2 decades of support experience. It's a guardrail for AI traffic where you can apply policies, redact PII and API keys, set model destinations, catch destructive actions before execution, etc. The whole thing is built with Claude and can also be configured and troubleshot via Claude/AI tools (it acts as an MCP server). It acts as a proxy for AI traffic. All you need is a Linux box (the Collector, where policy rules are applied) and a client app installed on the machine generating AI traffic to forward selected requests to it. Everything is visible in the UI. Lots of customization, with user experience kept in mind throughout. Happy to answer any questions!
